cells.tense: The meaning is moving through you now and you are the one moving it.
cells.ask: Pick one piece of what you carry, change how you hand it to fit the person in front of you, and watch whether it still lands.
cells.core:
The meaning is moving through you right now, and you are the one moving it. You pass something on and then you watch how it lands, and you change the wording before the next person gets it. That's the difference between keeping a thing alive and preserving it. You hold what you carry well enough to bend it and it doesn't break.

What else this openness can feed is up to you, and the offer will keep. The grip worth keeping is that the meaning keeps its shape in your hands while you turn it. What you want next is to put one piece of what you carry in front of someone in a shape that fits them, and watch whether it holds. The day after tells you more than the passing on does.

cells.tense: The meaning is being gripped so hard it will not survive the next pair of hands.
cells.ask: Say the thing once in the old words and again in your own, and leave the second one in the room without defending it.
cells.core:
You are holding the passed-on thing so hard it has stopped moving. Other people can feel the pressure in how it gets said, and something in them steps back. What you carry is solid enough to survive being said plainly; the grip isn't protecting it. Careful hands still pass things on; sealed windows don't, because nothing gets through them.

When structures fall in someone, the thing that was really worth keeping tends to stay standing on its own. Name one thing you believe deeply, say it once in the old words, and then say the same thing in words you'd actually use today. Leave it there without defending it. What survives that, you get to keep.

cells.tense: You came to the end of the old framework and no replacement took its place.
cells.ask: Find one piece of what you carry that still applies, write it down in three sentences, and send it to one person.
cells.core:
Nothing you were handed survived the collapse, and nothing replaced it. So you build the framework yourself, from nothing, and it works, but nothing gets to compound. Someone with the same problem has to solve it alone because nothing passed between you. Lonely isn't a mood here, it's what the situation looks like.

Under the thousand separate situations there tends to be one pattern that keeps appearing, and following it is what actually gets you out. Take one piece of what you carry that still applies, fold it into three plain sentences, and send it to one person. You are handing yourself something that lasts longer than one attempt.
cells.sheetLine: You start fresh each time and nothing gets to compound.

cells.tense: People are already taking things from you and calling them theirs.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you said that someone else is using, and say out loud, to one person, that it is yours and they can keep it.
cells.core:
People already walk off with things you say and use them later. That's the whole job. You just don't count it as a job, so it goes out under no name, and you reach the end of a week with nothing you remember doing.

Standing inside what you give is a steadier place than deciding whether you do it, and it isn't a decision anyone can make for you. Pick one thing you said that someone is using somewhere, and say out loud, to one person, that it's yours and they can keep it. The words exist on your side already. Saying them puts a name on the package.

attempts.check: The record supports the card, seat, status and medicine; the one claim it does not support is what actually went wrong earlier — so Too Little locates the person at the door without saying what happened there, who it was, how long ago, or what it cost. A reader could reasonably say the tradition they left was false and the seat was right to collapse it, so the cell leans on the lost shared ground, not on a judgment about the old one. The ask survives being wrong: picking up one workable piece and putting it where someone uses it teaches something even if the read missed. The sentence that serves me more than them is anything that turns the orphaned position into a flattering gift, so it is cut.
